newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SILENCE MARKS SACCHI'S RETURN TO SERIE A FOOTBALL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SILENCE MARKS SACCHI'S RETURN TO SERIE A FOOTBALL.

text.p: If Arrigo Sacchi were looking for some peace and quiet when he left Italy's national side to coach Milan, he can take heart from a 2-1 win over Udinese on Sunday.
As the white-haired coach walked into the San Siro for his first taste of serie A soccer in five years, he was met with the eerie sound of silence.
Shocked by Milan's humiliation at the hands of Norway's Rosenborg in the European Cup on Wednesday, diehard fans decided to let their banners do the talking.
"No scapegoats. You're all guilty," said one banner, delivering its verdict on Milan's fall from grace.

Called on to select a Milan team for the first time since May 1991, Sacchi dropped goalkeeper Sebastiano Rossi, whose errors cost Milan dear against Rosenborg, and brought back George Weah and Marcel Desailly.
But in the first half, his side looked as poor as Wednesday's, although Zvonimir Boban saw his 19th minute shot hit both posts before running to safety.

After the break, however, Sacchi showed his old touch for conjuring success out of adversity by sending on Dejan Savicevic. Within nine minutes, the Montenegrin had headed home Weah's cross -- with the help of the crossbar.
At this stage Giovanni Stroppa, a mainstay in Sacchi's old Milan, threatened to gatecrash his former boss's party -- unleashing a freekick into the top corner.
Showing the resilience that has been missing of late, Milan edged in front again in the 67th minute with a well-taken goal from Stefano Eranio - again made by Weah.
But Milan's penchant for making life difficult for themselves this season returned to haunt the final five minutes.
In the 85th minute, Alessandro Costacurta was booked for a foul, and then sent off for kicking the player - Diego Caverzan - on the ground.
In a hectic finale, Angelo Pagotto saved the day with a double save from Paolo Poggi.
Victory brought the champions' run of eight league and cup matches without a win to a halt.
"I'm satisfied," said club president Silvio Berlusconi, praising the second-half debut of new signing Jesper Blomqvist of Sweden, "you can already see Sacchi's touch."
"The important thing for Milan today was to regain confidence in themselves," said Sacchi, "but if this was the real Milan, then we face a tough year."

It is testimony to the lack of consistency among Italy's leading teams this season that, despite one of their worst runs in recent history, Milan are still just four points behind leaders Vicenza and Juventus.
But European and World club champions Juve finally look poised to assert their authority on the title race after winning 1-0 at Sampdoria.

The win, courtesy of Ciro Ferrara's well-taken 33rd minute goal from Zinedine Zidane's corner, means the Turin club now trail Vicenza, held 1-1 at home to Inter, on goal difference alone with a game in hand.
Marcello Lippi's side can take command if they win at Udinese in a league match scheduled for Wednesday.

Vicenza, leading serie A for the first time in their 94-year history, were left to rue a series of squandered chances after midfielder Giampiero Maini had given them an 18th minute lead against Inter.
Superb goalkeeping from Gianluca Pagliuca and some wayward finishing allowed Inter's French playmaker Youri Djorkaeff to level from the penalty spot in the 63rd minute.
Roy Hodgson's Inter, beaten just once this season, like third on 21 points, one behind Juve and Vicenza and one ahead of Napoli and Bologna.
Napoli, enjoying one of their best seasons since the departure of Maradona in 1991, needed a last minute goal from Mauro Milanese to see off lowly Verona.

Bologna, first division champions last season, looked set for a share of first place after Michele Paramatti's 54th minute opener against Piacenza made amends for Igor Kolyvanov's penalty miss a minute earlier.
But, with the referee poised to blow the final whistle, Andrea Tentoni levelled the score for the visitors.
